top_signal.title: The customer says “I'll think about it.” Does your attitude change?
top_signal.summary: Imagine a customer comes into a phone shop. You ask what they use their phone for, what bothers them about the old one, and what they're comfortable spending. After talking, you recommend a cheaper model because it already meets their needs.   You explain why. They ask a few questions, then say, “Thanks. I'll think about it.”   That's the part I find interesting. Do you answer their last question just as helpfully, or do your replies get shorter once a sale seems unlikely?   I think about B2C sales as three steps: connect, understand, then sell. But if the friendliness disappears when someone isn't ready to buy, I wonder how genuine the first step was.   Of course, being sincere doesn't mean giving unlimited advice. There are other customers to help and a business to run. You can politely end a conversation without becoming cold.   The harder part is accepting that this person might never return, refer anyone, or buy later. There may be no satisfying ending where treating them well turns out to have been profitable.   I'd still want the first two steps to count, even when the third one doesn't happen.       submitted by     /u/oky_sabeni       [link]       [comments]
